title: Directing Vision Transformer Attention to Emotion-Relevant Facial Regions for Facial Expression Recognition
content: Facial expression recognition (FER) in unconstrained images is difficult because faces vary widely in pose, illumination, and occlusion, and several expressions are visually similar. Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently set strong FER benchmarks, yet they share a structural limitation that every image patch is treated equally, so the model holds no built-in prior for which facial regions carry expressive information. This paper introduces KGAB-ViT (Keypoint-Guided Attention Bias Vision Transformer), which injects a facial-anatomy prior directly into the backbone by adding compact Gaussian keypoint heatmaps as an additive bias to the attention logits of each active encoder layer. A learnable per-layer gate regulates how strongly the keypoints steer attention, allowing early layers to refine generic features while deeper layers concentrate on expressive regions. To identify where keypoint injection is most effective, we further define and compare two variants—KGPE-ViT, which adds the prior to the positional encoding, and KGP-ViT, which replaces the positional encoding with it. On AffectNet-8, KGAB-ViT attains 72.27% top-1 accuracy, exceeding prior reported results on this benchmark while adding only about 1,500 parameters.
